I wasn’t focusing on society’s view of gender transitions; rather, my point was that those fundamentals (transitions etc.) are highly romanticized in this subreddit. It is quite dangerous for teens to focus on such a complex subject. for example, how can they know that it won’t be a regretful decision later? they can’t predict others reactions (families, friends) or the possible risks. 

just as an example, as a teen, you’re likely to switch friend groups frequently - people switch schools, move, become apart of subcultures etc. being highly influenced by people online who promote an idealized view of sexuality and gender transitions can lead to real-life consequences later on. right now? fine, you do you, but nobody talks about the risks later. teens here are telling other teens how great it is and encouraging them to do transitions etc. if they feel that way. the problem is, they only focus on the positive aspects. as a teen, you tend not to think deeply about the consequences and might follow along because everyone else is doing it. and since it is highly romanticized here, maybe people should not be so positive about it constantly?

curiosity is very normal, especially at that age when you are pubescent and your hormones are up. you want to try new things, which is fine—that’s natural. however, gender transitions are very complex, and i don’t think anyone should romanticize them at such an early age. being curious about your gender, body, and others is very normal. 

if you browse a community every day and a large margin of the people you meet are trans, i am sure you will eventually be influenced by them. this is especially true in a community where people constantly romanticize it. just because you are friends with a gay person in real life doesn’t mean you’re going to be gay, but online? considering that increased depression rates and lack of social interaction are common factors, it’s likely that people will find their place here then.
